SddAmplifySecurity.keywords: security, amplify, threat-model, trust-boundaries, authn, authz, secrets, input-validation, pii, data-classification, sca, sdd-amplify-security
SddAmplifySecurity.Mission:
Deepen the security posture of a scope spec under discovery — threat model lite: trust boundaries, authn/authz model, secrets handling, input validation at external boundaries, PII / data classification, dependency risk (delegated to SCA tooling). Loaded lazily by the discovery interview's triage when the scope touches external input, user accounts, or sensitive data; inherits the session core (language, dialogue, safeguard, no-narration) — not repeated here.
Input — the scope spec draft + interview context. Output — ordinary flat requirement entries in the canonical Requirements section + follow-up items appended to the discovery interview map. Out of scope: pentest planning and infra-hardening runbooks — detailed material belongs in Architecture or one referenced supporting section only when genuinely needed.
SddAmplifySecurity.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): QUESTION_FORMAT
An amplification opens with a ready answer, not a questionnaire. FIRST assemble a complete defaults package — the decisions live products of this class actually ship with (run a short targeted research pass when class practice is uncertain, grounded in the scope's intent) — and present it as ONE accept-or-edit reply: the operator takes everything with one word or edits by item number. Ask via the AskUserQuestion / multi-question tool when available; fallback `QUESTION_FORMAT`. Deep-dive questions open only for topics the operator explicitly marks deep-dive; every untouched topic keeps its default. An accepted default is a real decision — record it like one.
Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
Every input crossing a trust boundary into the system — user input, webhook, file upload, inter-service call, queue message — is untrusted until validated at that boundary. Validation lives at the boundary itself; inner layers receive already-typed, already-checked data. A spec that names a trust boundary MUST name the validation applied at it.
Secrets never committed. On leak: rotate first, rewrite history second.
**Prevention:** - `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.*.local` always gitignored (`AX_GITIGNORE_BASELINE`). - `.env.example` tracked with placeholder values to document required keys. - Pre-commit hook scans staged files for secret patterns (recommended: `gitleaks`, `detect-secrets`, `trufflehog`). - Code review checks for hardcoded credentials in any file extension.
**On leak detection:** 1. **Rotate the leaked credential immediately** (revoke + reissue). The credential is compromised the moment it hits a remote, regardless of subsequent rewrite. 2. Document incident: what leaked, when, who rotated, what notifications went out. 3. Optional: `git filter-repo` or BFG to scrub history, then force-push (coordinate with team).
Git history is forever. Once a secret reaches the remote, assume it's harvested by scanners within minutes. Rotation is mandatory; history rewrite is hygiene, not security.
SddAmplifySecurity.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_SECURITY_SURFACE` | Triage misfired: no trust boundary, no stored user data — report and return control | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_DEFAULTS` | Operator declines the whole defaults package and skips deep-dive — leave the spec untouched |

Step.Goal: Assemble the security defaults package for this product class.
Step.Action: From the spec draft, map the attack surface: trust boundaries, entry points, stored data classes. Per `AX_AMPLIFY_DEFAULTS_FIRST`, draft one observable outcome per relevant topic — boundaries + validation (per `AX_EXTERNAL_INPUT_UNTRUSTED`), authn/authz model, secrets handling (per `AX_SECRETS_DISCIPLINE`), PII classification, SCA delegation — grounded in what live products of this class ship; short targeted research when class practice is uncertain. A topic with no observable product constraint is not an entry. Zero surface found → `H_NO_SECURITY_SURFACE`.

Step.Goal: One accept-or-edit gate; deep-dive only on explicit pick.
Step.Action: Present the package as ONE reply per `AX_AMPLIFY_DEFAULTS_FIRST` (AskUserQuestion when available, else `QUESTION_FORMAT`); each topic accept / edit / deep-dive. For topics the operator marks deep-dive, interview by the topic map: boundaries → authn/authz → secrets → validation → PII → dependencies. Untouched topics keep their defaults. STOP.

Step.Goal: Write the agreed outcomes as current-format requirements.
Step.Action:
`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/requirement-entry-format.xml")`. Continue the spec's next unused sequential `-REQ-` IDs. Write one ordinary flat entry per accepted observable outcome, with modality class, behaviour sentence, and short `Constraint`, `Verification`, and `Trace` lines. Never create `### Security`, another topic heading, or a table inside Requirements.
If the existing Requirements section is legacy split/topic format, read it as input and migrate the whole section to flat entries in this already-approved edit; preserve every still-valid outcome and do not leave a mixed representation or ask for a second approval. A threat/data-classification table belongs in Architecture by default, or in one explicitly named supporting section outside Requirements only when the detail is genuinely needed; link it from `Trace`. Non-default picks and notable accepted defaults → Decision Log per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`. Unresolved topics → discovery interview map, not vague requirements. Return control to the interview.
